key_insight: LLM agent failures are predictable very early from hidden activations, enabling safe early-abort decisions before wasted compute accumulates.
engineering_relevance: A recall-controlled probe cascade can cut inference cost substantially while preserving a user-specified success recall, making it practical for deployment in multi-step agent systems.
method: Train lightweight per-round probes on agent hidden states to predict eventual episode failure.
Use distribution-free calibrated gates with jointly searched per-round recall budgets to enforce a global episode-level recall target.
Abort episodes that are predicted doomed while allowing eventually successful episodes to pass all gates at the desired rate.
evidence_signal: Across two agent models on TextCraft, the cascade met 90%–97% recall targets and at the 90% target saved 47.1% ± 10.3% compute for Qwen-2.5-7B and 37.2% ± 8.8% for Llama-3.2-3B.
watch_item: High-recall guarantees depend on sufficient calibration data, and the paper notes that some recall targets may be impossible to certify with the available sample size.
paper_title: Doomed from the Start: Early Abort of LLM Agent Episodes via a Recall-Controlled Probe Cascade
